title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: AUGIE'S BREAD
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Augie Barnes, a water plant operator in Roanoke, Virginia.
He kept a whole city's water clean, but he bought his bread at the gas station.
Then a neighbor handed him a jar, and his life started to rise.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: THE DOORSTOP
segments.quote: Every adversity, every failure, every heartache carries with it the seed of an equal or greater benefit.
segments.author: Napoleon Hill
lines: His neighbor Lorraine, a retired baker, was moving to Tampa.
She handed him a jar of sourdough starter named Gertrude. Fifty years old. Feed her every day.
His first loaf came out like a brick. It became a doorstop.
Then he remembered a line from Napoleon Hill:
Every adversity, every failure, every heartache carries with it the seed of an equal or greater benefit.
So he called Lorraine. She laughed, then told him what went wrong.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: EVERY NIGHT
segments.quote: Patience and diligence, like faith, remove mountains.
segments.author: William Penn
lines: Augie taped a line from William Penn, the founder of Pennsylvania, to his locker:
Patience and diligence, like faith, remove mountains.
So every night after his shift, he fed Gertrude and baked one loaf.
His wife Denise said the kitchen smelled like a bakery, and looked like a storm hit one.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: THE RISE
segments.quote: Patience is a necessary ingredient of genius.
segments.author: Benjamin Disraeli
lines: By March, the bread was better, but heavy. Augie kept rushing it.
Lorraine said, Honey, you can't hurry dough, and quoted Benjamin Disraeli, the British prime minister:
Patience is a necessary ingredient of genius.
So he let the dough rise all night. Next morning, the crust crackled. He danced in his socks.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: ACROSS THE STREET
segments.quote: Only a life lived for others is a life worthwhile.
segments.author: Albert Einstein
lines: Across the street, Ray Whitlow had been laid off after twenty-six years. He stopped mowing. Stopped waving.
Augie had two loaves, and a line from Albert Einstein in his head:
Only a life lived for others is a life worthwhile.
So he walked over a warm loaf. Next morning, Ray was mowing. And waving.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: THE MARKET
segments.quote: Patience is the art of hoping.
segments.author: Vauvenargues
lines: In May, Augie rented a farmers market table. He sold three loaves. Two to Denise's sisters.
He wanted to quit. But Ray, now his helper, quoted the French writer Vauvenargues:
Patience is the art of hoping.
So Augie came back every Saturday. By October, he sold out by nine.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: THE JARS
segments.quote: Be not simply good; be good for something.
segments.author: Henry David Thoreau
lines: Folks wanted his secret. So he split Gertrude into little jars, with a Henry David Thoreau line on every lid:
Be not simply good; be good for something.
He gave away fifty. Ray got hired at a bakery downtown.
And Lorraine? Augie mails her a loaf every month. She grades it. He's up to a B plus.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Learn from the flop. Show up. Let it rise. Share it. Keep hoping. Be useful.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Learn from the flop. Show up. Let it rise. Share it. Keep hoping. Be good for something.
Me? I baked bread once. The ducks still won't talk to me.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night.
